unsupported_codes.reason: Overweight and obesity: reporting a code from this category makes a diagnosis from the height, weight and body mass index in the vital signs; the provider states no such diagnosis.
Body mass index: a BMI code is assigned only with an associated diagnosis documented by the patient's provider, and the note has none.

citations.M16.12: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting FY2027, Section I.A.19: the assignment of a diagnosis code is based on the provider's diagnostic statement that the condition exists. Section I.B.14: a body mass index may be taken from the documentation of a clinician other than the patient's provider, but the associated diagnosis, such as overweight or obesity, must be documented by the patient's provider. Section I.C.21.c.3: BMI codes should only be assigned when there is an associated, reportable diagnosis documented by the patient's provider. Here the surgeon's diagnosis is primary osteoarthritis of the left hip; the body mass index of 41.2 is recorded by the medical assistant and the surgeon documents no weight-related diagnosis, so the osteoarthritis is reported alone.

coder_notes: The right hip is documented as normal, so the osteoarthritis is unilateral. Hip pain and the antalgic gait are part of the osteoarthritis. The preoperative evaluation is requested, not done at this visit, so no preoperative examination code is reported. Acetaminophen is taken as needed. In practice this documentation would lead to a provider query; the gold is what can be reported from the note as written.
